from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
p = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,14):

strengths: The paper addresses an important bottleneck in multimodal inference through a simple module that reuses vision-encoder attention and key features. Combining adaptive token selection with information recovery through merging is practically appealing.

Reducing 576 visual tokens to approximately 40 is substantial. Evaluation covers six benchmarks and both 7B and 13B LLaVA-1.5 models, demonstrating that considerable task-relevant information survives this compression. The fine-tuned 7B model preserves or improves ScienceQA and POPE scores.

The ablations provide useful supporting evidence: training-free PruMerge achieves 54.00 on TextVQA versus 47.96 for the best reported spatial-sampling configuration, and Table 4 shows improvements from adding token supplementation.
The overall pipeline is understandable, foundational methods and datasets are cited, and the limitations section acknowledges lossy compression and restricted validation scope.
weaknesses: The claim of broadly comparable performance understates substantial losses. Table 1 shows VQAv2 falling from 78.5 to 72.0 for 7B and from 80.0 to 72.8 for 13B; 7B MME falls from 1510.7 to 1350.3, and 13B MMBench from 67.7 to 62.3. These losses could represent a useful efficiency tradeoff, but accuracy-versus-cost curves are needed to substantiate that tradeoff. Without fine-tuning, POPE also drops from 85.9 to 76.2.

The experiments do not establish the distinctive benefit of the proposed combination over stronger alternatives. Table 3 mainly compares against selecting the first tokens and uniform spatial sampling. Missing comparisons include fixed-budget top-attention selection and established token-merging methods at matched budgets. Since attention-based pruning and key-based merging build closely on cited prior work, these controls are important for assessing originality and the value of IQR-based adaptivity.

The efficiency evidence is limited to roofline estimates of LLM prefill under one assumed prompt length. There are no measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or peak-memory results accounting for the vision encoder, selection/merging overhead, autoregressive decoding, and variable token counts during batching. The theoretical savings are promising but do not establish practical acceleration.

Important implementation details remain ambiguous. Algorithm 1 does not specify the neighborhood size k or attention-head aggregation. Its update excludes the selected center from the candidate neighbors and uses an unnormalized weighted sum, whereas the text describes supplementing retained tokens through weighted averaging. Cluster overlap and key normalization are also unclear. These choices can materially change the resulting features and hinder reproduction.

The training controls are incomplete. Main results use an additional LoRA fine-tuning epoch, while the sampling comparisons are training-free; corresponding fine-tuned sampling baselines and a full-token model receiving the same additional training are absent. LoRA configuration and optimization settings are also unspecified. Consequently, the experiments do not fully separate the benefits of the reduction mechanism from adaptation to the altered inputs.
